result:
I played all 24 months. All three training runs were met, there were no penalties and no unserved inference, and the final **net cost was $996.2M**.

**Settlement:** spend $1,138.8M − mark-to-market $261.8M + remaining obligations $119.2M = $996.2M.

| Window | Done / needed |
|---|---|
| Months 0–7 | 97.4 / 60 |
| Months 8–15 | 188.5 / 140 |
| Months 16–23 | ~320 / 320 (301.9 after month 22, 18.1 needed in month 23) |

**How it went:**
- **Months 0–3:** I bought 24k H GPUs from the vendor plus 2k from broker A, and signed 50 MW of extra power. GPUs sat idle until month 6 because power was short.
- **Months 8–10:** window 2 had spare capacity, so I sold 9k H before the launch cut used-H value by 40%.
- **Window 3:** the launch rumours (18, 15, 18, 17) only fit month 16 or 17. With no launch or confirmation at 16, I expected 17. When gen N launched in month 17, I took 25 kH of 6-month reserved capacity (the cheapest option per kH-month), 4k N from broker A and 6k N from the vendor. In the last four months I sold off the surplus.
- **Brokers:** I only used broker A, and it delivered both orders. Broker B was never tested.

**What cost the most:**
- **Too much compute in windows 1 and 2.** Window 1 finished with 37 kH-months more than needed and window 2 with 48. Compute only counts in its own window, so that surplus was wasted.
- **Power ($205M).** I signed more than I needed, and contracts running past month 23 are still charged at settlement.
- **One unneeded hedge.** The 5 kH reservation in month 18 turned out to be unnecessary.

I kept a belief log every month. Two notes (months 4 and 19) were cut short because a semicolon inside the note split it into a separate command. Neither error took effect, and the month's real actions still ran.
